newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Departing Patten lists things to miss about HK.
newsitem.headline: Departing Patten lists things to miss about HK.

text.p: Piles of ageing eggs, squawking hens and guinea fowls, caged grasshoppers and much, much more are on the nostalgia list of outgoing Hong Kong governor Chris Patten.

"The string sacks full of frogs as black as your hat, the squirming eels, the great slabs of tuna, the wonderful fish sliced right down the middle with the life still pumping in them. Ah, what a sight," Patten told The South China Morning Post.

In an article published on Monday, the last day of British colonial rule, Patten exulted about tools he found at the top of Possession Street, the spot where the Britain planted its flag 156 years ago.
"There are thermos flasks, There are woks. There are gardening gloves. There are secateurs. All the things that make an ironmongers so much fun," Patten said.
Patten said he would also miss Andy Ng, an antique dealer who "taught me more than anybody else about Chinese arts and crafts".
"One thing I will miss will be that fantastic exotic rambling through these bazaars of this, the greatest maritime Chinese city," said Patten.
He also said he would miss assorted civil servants, a tennis partner, his personal assistant, the proprietor of his favourite restaurant and a chief steward who gave Patten race tips.
Patten's term as Hong Kong governor ends at midnight (1600 GMT), when Britain's Prince Charles will formally hand back Hong Kong to Chinese President Jiang Zemin.
Patten will then leave Hong Kong aboard the Royal Yacht Britannia with Prince Charles.
